channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario refers concerns about OSAP payments at private career colleges to OPP
Doug Ford wants to delay parole eligibility for anyone convicted of murdering a police officer
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says that anyone convicted of murdering a police officer shouldn’t be eligible for parole for a period of 30 years.

item.title: Secondary students are now graded based on attendance but some say confusion remains
item.description: New provincial legislation that makes attendance and participation a part of the final grade for secondary school students is now in effect but a representative from an association representing student trustees says that there continues to be uncertainty around 'grey areas.'

item.title: OLP leadership candidate Eric Lombardi withdraws from race
item.description: Ontario Liberal Party leadership candidate Eric Lombardi has ended his campaign.

item.title: Ontario ministers defend secret payout to Elon Musk's SpaceX over nixed Starlink deal
item.description: Ontario ministers defended keeping secret the province’s payout to Elon Musk’s SpaceX over a cancelled Starlink contract, as critics accused the government of obfuscation during the recent release of its latest financial statements.

item.title: Affordable child-care program extended in Ontario, but not to $10 a day
item.description: Ontario and the federal government have agreed to extend the national affordable child-care program in the province for another four years, but it comes with no promises of further lowering the fees parents pay.

item.title: Ontario transparency watchdog warns government is dodging its orders
item.description: Ontario’s transparency watchdog is warning that the government is dodging its orders more frequently, including orders that would shed light on how a multi-billion dollar government fund pushed grants to supporters including one to an adult entertainment club.

item.title: Health ministers to hold emergency meeting to discuss federal funding ahead of budget
item.description: Ontario’s health minister says she and her colleagues from across the country are set to hold an emergency meeting to talk about federal funding.

item.title: Queen’s Park officer dies in weekend collision
item.description: A Queen’s Park peace officer died in a motor vehicle collision over the weekend.

item.title: Premier Ford not worried about Volkswagen battery plant delay
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Friday he is not worried about a two-year delay in the opening of a massive Volkswagen electric vehicle battery plant in southwestern Ontario.

item.title: Ontario public high school teachers to hold strike vote amid stalled bargaining
item.description: All of Ontario’s major education unions are holding strike votes in November, hopeful that strong mandates will lead to progress at the bargaining table.

item.title: Ontario announces $1M donation to support Ukrainian energy infrastructure
item.description: The Ontario government has announced a $1-million donation to Ukraine as Russia’s invasion of the country nears the five-year mark.

item.title: Ontario deficit in 2025-26 better than projected at $13 billion, province says
item.description: Ontario says its deficit is slightly better than initially projected.

item.title: Ontario to standardize truck driver training after scathing auditor general report
item.description: Ontario is introducing standardized entry-level training for commercial truck drivers.

item.title: Ford will not endorse any Toronto mayoral candidate: premier’s office
item.description: A day after Ontario Premier Doug Ford said he supports Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow amid her bid for re-election, his office says it was not an endorsement.
